approach: Root cause, from the code: `checks::failure_section` (checks.rs:373-419) is the one place a failed check's output is chosen for storage, and it knows only two things: a runner marker (`failures:`, `panicked at`, `---- x stdout ----`, `test result: FAILED`, checks.rs:354-360) and a cleanup HEADER line (`Post job cleanup`, `Post Run `, `Cleaning up orphan processes`, checks.rs:345-351). It never reads the lines `cargo xtask test-shard` prints to name the failing unit: `== shard k/n: <unit>` before each unit (xtask/src/shard.rs:317, main.rs:112-114), and `error: shard k of n: X of Y units failed: a; b` at the end (shard.rs:332-337, main.rs:64). The shard runs every unit even after one fails (shard.rs:315-327), so a failing unit's output is followed by whole passing units, and the plain 200-line tail or the jump case (checks.rs:402-418) keeps the passing units' lines, not the failing unit's. A log whose cleanup block has no recognised header (cancelled or cut-off log, git credential-removal lines above the header) falls through to a plain tail of cleanup text, and nothing tells the reader that no failing section was found. Header-first cutting landed in fe42b01 (HISTORY.txt:733); `records/` is absent from the snapshot, so which shape each of the six jobs' logs had cannot be shown, and the plan fixes both shapes without claiming which job had which. Fix, three parts in the four code files. (A) gh/client.rs: `failed_units_only(log)`, next to `failing_units` (client.rs:264), reads the log's last `units failed:` summary and, for any log whose summary names a unit that has a `== shard` header (no condition on runner markers), keeps each named unit's own part whole, collapses every run of other units to one `(output of N passing units not kept: ...)` line, and keeps the summary and what follows. `detail_from_job_logs` passes that reduced log to `failure_section`. (B) checks.rs: cleanup is recognised by content as well as by header, in `is_cleanup_line`, the single recogniser, using a bounded backward walk from the end of the log. A log with no failing section keeps its last pre-cleanup lines plus ONE trailing note. A non-empty log that held only cleanup becomes an explicit `no output was kept` note. (C) send_back.rs: `CheckFailure::of` passes the stored output through `failure_section`. routing.rs gets tests only. No record shape, admission or gate changes, and no refusal rule is added, so 0% of past accepted readings are newly refused.

decisions.choice: Read the failing unit from the log's own summary and keep its output, whether or not it holds a runner marker. In gh/client.rs add `summary_units(line) -> Option<Vec<&str>>` (after an optional `error: `, the trimmed line starts `shard ` and holds ` units failed: `; the units are the text after it, split on `; `) and `failed_units_only(log: &str) -> Option<String>`. It takes the LAST summary line, finds the `== shard k/n: <unit>` header lines before it (the same `strip_prefix("== shard ")` and `split_once(": ")` that `failing_units` uses at client.rs:267-269), and returns None when no named unit has a header. Otherwise it keeps each named unit's part whole, from its header to the next header or the summary line, with its markers. Each run of unnamed units becomes one line `(output of N passing units not kept: a; b)` (`unit` for N=1; at most 6 names, then `; +M more`). Lines before the first header are dropped. The summary line and every line after it (`##[error]`, cleanup) are kept. The precondition `!has_failing_section(log)` of the earlier plan is removed. `detail_from_job_logs` calls `failure_section` on the reduced log.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 1. The information the failing stage lacked is which unit failed, and the log states it. Mechanism on the base tree, read at checks.rs:380-418: a marker unit followed by about 1000 lines of passing units has no marker in the last 200 lines, so the jump case keeps about 180 lines from the first marker, a `…` line and the last 20 lines. The verifier brief quotes the last 60 lines (briefs.rs:1110, `clip_log_tail` 1114-1116) and the send-back the last 3000 bytes (send_back.rs:297), so both show passing-unit lines and not the assertion text. After the reduction the log is the failing unit's part, one collapse line and the summary, so the marker is within the window and within the last 60 lines. A passing unit that prints `panicked at` (a child process's stderr) is dropped, which answers finding 4 for every log that has a summary. Existing fixtures are unchanged because none has a summary: grep of `units failed` over the repository's .rs files finds only xtask/src/shard.rs:264 and :333; gh/tests.rs:386-405 `shard_log` and run/tests.rs:7724-7734 `SHARD_LOG` end at `error: test failed`, and shard.rs:263-267 prints `N units failed, so their times...` (comma, no `shard ` prefix), which `summary_units` does not match. The reduction sits in client.rs before `failure_section`, so `failure_section` stays a string cutter used by local runs and by `with_failure_detail`, and no cleanup recogniser is added outside checks.rs. A failing part longer than the shard's window loses its first lines (a risk).

Finding 1 shows the base-tree jump case then shows passing-unit lines (checks.rs:402-418). Its stated reason was also wrong: no existing fixture has a summary, so None already covers all of them.

decisions.choice: One cleanup recogniser, in checks.rs. Split `is_cleanup_header` (the three existing forms, `##[group]` prefix ignored) out of `is_cleanup_line`. `is_cleanup_line` becomes header or content: `[command]/usr/bin/git `, `Temporarily overriding HOME`, `Adding repository directory to the temporary git global config`, `Removing HTTP extra header`, `Removing includeIf`, `Complete job`, `Evaluate and set job outputs`, `##[warning]Node.js`. The bare `/usr/bin/git ` form is not matched. The doc comment becomes 'any line of CI runner cleanup text, not only the one that starts the block'. `failure_section` sets `anchor` (last runner marker, else last `##[error]` line) and `floor = anchor + 1`, else 0. It then cuts at the first `is_cleanup_header` line at or after `floor`, else the end, and `cleanup_start(lines, floor)` walks back from that point over blank lines, recognised lines and at most `CLEANUP_GAP = 1` consecutive unrecognised lines. It stops at a `##[group]Run ` step start, at `floor`, or at the second unrecognised line, and returns the earliest recognised line reached. The block is cut from there.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 2 and carries the earlier answers. The real checkout post block interleaves single plain lines (`git version 2.x`, an `extraheader` key line) between `[command]/usr/bin/git ...` lines, which a gap of 1 covers. Only the `[command]` form is a cited form; no cited log has a bare `/usr/bin/git ` line, and `failure_section` also runs on local output (checks.rs:618), so the bare form is not matched. Finding 2's fixture error is fixed in the demonstrations: criterion 2 test (a) uses only `[command]/usr/bin/git ...`, `Removing HTTP extra header`, `Cleaning up orphan processes` and `##[warning]Node.js 20`. Walking from the END can strip only a trailing block, so checkout lines at the start of a log are never chosen. The step-start boundary separates the checkout block from the failing step. Idempotence: after a pass the last kept non-blank lines are two unrecognised lines, a step start or `floor`, so a second pass (with_failure_detail on a stored tail, CheckFailure::of) cuts nothing. Input forms and tests are listed in the criterion 1 demonstration. The existing tests at checks.rs:857, 867, 879, 892, 906 and 921 are traced to be unchanged: each ends in `##[error]` or two unrecognised lines before the first header, so `cleanup_start` returns None.

rejected.option: Keep the bare `/usr/bin/git ` prefix

rejected.why: They wrap every step of a job log.

rejected.why: Criterion 4 forbids it, and the local run (checks.rs:618) would not get it.

decisions.choice: The 'no failing section' note is ONE line at the END of the whole stored tail: `(no failing test section was found in <shard>[, <shard>...][, +N more]; for each, the lines kept are the last of its log before the runner's cleanup)`. checks.rs supplies `has_failing_section(text)` (any runner marker), `no_test_section_note(&[&str])`, `NO_TEST_SECTION_PREFIX` and `NO_OUTPUT_NOTE`. In `detail_from_job_logs`, per readable shard: `found = reduced.is_some() || has_failing_section(&section)`, computed on the stored section and not on the raw log. A shard is named in the note when `!found && (conclusion != "failure" || section.trim_end() != log.trim_end())`. Before sizing, the code reserves 1 line and the byte length of a note naming every readable shard with no reduction (a superset of the shards that can be named), plus 1 line for the `failing units:` line when `!names.is_empty() && !units.is_empty()`: `per_lines = ((200 - reserved) / n).saturating_sub(header).max(1)`, `per_bytes = FAILED_TAIL_BYTES.saturating_sub(note_len) / n`.
decisions.reason: Answers findings 3 and 4. Finding 3: the behavioral reason for the second clause is that a log stored whole was not cut, so every line is visible and a note saying lines were cut would be false. A shard that did not finish (any conclusion but `failure`) or whose cleanup or older lines were cut always gets the note. The reason goes in the code comment and the CHANGELOG, and gh/tests.rs:578-590 (a two-line `failure` log, `ends_with("build broke\n")`) is untouched as a consequence. Finding 4: `found` no longer reads the raw log. With a summary the reduced log is the evidence, so a stray `panicked at` in a passing unit's output cannot turn the note off. For a log with no summary the stored section is used, which can differ from the raw log only when the marker was cut by the window. A stray marker kept by the jump case (checks.rs:402-418) still counts as found; that is behavior the base tree already has, and it is listed as a risk. The note is the last line so it survives every tail reader: failure_section keeps the end (checks.rs:394-406, 417-418), CheckFailure::of keeps the last 3000 bytes (send_back.rs:297), the verifier brief the last 60 lines (briefs.rs:1110-1127) after `check_result_view` strips only a leading units line (verify.rs:75-86). Three shards give 3 x (65 + 1 header) + 1 note = 199 lines, and with the units line 200, so with_failure_detail's second pass (checks.rs:443-445, limit 199 after a units line) drops nothing. Reserving the units line moves a first-pass window from 200 to 199 only where a units line exists; the second pass already cut it to 199, so the stored count is unchanged.

decisions.choice: Leave the second pass of `with_failure_detail` (checks.rs:436-446) as it is, and state its multi-shard edge in Risks.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 5. The second pass recomputes the anchor over the combined `== <job>` text and cuts at the first cleanup header at or after it. A header that a shard's first pass kept (because it came before that shard's own anchor) can sit after the combined anchor taken from an EARLIER shard only when a later shard has no marker. The cut would then drop that shard's rest and the trailing note. The input needs a cleanup-looking header inside a failing step's output plus two or more shards of which the later one has no marker, and the loss is bounded to the stored tail text; `failed_tests` and the units line are unaffected. Skipping the second pass for note-ending text would add a branch to a function used by all reused records for a rare input, so the edge is stated and not coded around.

risks.risk: A failing unit's part longer than the shard's window (199 lines for one shard, about 65 for three) loses its first lines in the stored tail. The send-back keeps only the last 3000 bytes, so a long part can lose its start there.
risks.mitigation: The reduced log drops every other unit, so the window holds only failing parts, one collapse line and the summary. A failing part's marker section is normally in its last lines, which the tail keeps. The send-back byte limit is not caused by cleanup text and is left unchanged.

risks.risk: A log with no summary line (a cancelled or cut-off shard) that holds a stray `panicked at` early on is read as having a section: the jump case (checks.rs:402-418, base behavior) keeps the head from that line, `found` is true, and no note is added.
risks.mitigation: Not caused by cleanup text and unchanged from the base tree. With a summary, the reduction drops passing units' text, so the stray line cannot count. Stated in the CHANGELOG as a limit.

risks.risk: Finding 5's edge: in `with_failure_detail`'s second pass over a combined multi-shard text, a cleanup header kept inside one shard's section (because it came before that shard's own anchor) can sit after the combined anchor taken from an earlier shard when a later shard has no marker. The cut then drops that shard's rest and the trailing note from the stored tail.
risks.mitigation: It needs a cleanup-looking header inside a failing step's output and two or more shards, with the one holding the header after the last marker. The loss is limited to stored tail text; `failed_tests` and the units line are unaffected. Not coded around, to keep `with_failure_detail` free of a special case; stated here and not tested.

risks.risk: Stored records written before the change still hold cleanup text.
risks.mitigation: They are not rewritten. The send-back view re-cleans them through `failure_section`; the other readers show the old text.

demonstrations.method: Read the new entry under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Fixed`, inserted after the entry that ends at CHANGELOG.md:23 (the Hestia entry) and before `### Added` (CHANGELOG.md:25).
demonstrations.observes: One added entry. It names the failure class `failed-check-output-is-ci-noise-cause-of-test-failure-invisible` and the jobs 20261106-022423-vdtn, 20261106-045349-f6x6 and 20261027-054225-ycks. It states the root cause as what the code did and dates the earlier header fix (fe42b01, 2026-11-07): `failure_section` knew only runner markers and a cleanup header; the `== shard` lines and the `units failed:` summary that name the failing unit were not read, so a failing unit's output gave way to the last 200 lines of later passing units; a block with no recognised header, or with git credential-removal lines above the header, fell through to a plain tail of cleanup text; nothing said that no failing section was found. It says what the record stores now: the failing unit's own output with the passing units collapsed to one line (marker or no marker), or the failing section, or the last pre-cleanup lines with one trailing note naming the shards with no failing test section, with no note when the whole log was kept because nothing was cut; the no-output note only when a non-empty log held only cleanup; empty output unchanged. It says recognition is by known text, so unknown cleanup forms can still appear, that the reduction reads the text `xtask test-shard` prints and does nothing when that text changes, and that a stray marker in a log with no summary still counts as a section. It states that the logs of the six jobs were not available, so no claim is made about their shape. It states no refusal rule is added (0% of readings newly refused) and that the drain test and a base-tree rerun are not part of the change. It lists the tests with their commands and states only what the diff does.
